correctness.rationale: Conditional posterior has exactly two constant densities; exact two-outcome conditional moments give the information objective. A signed rational mirror difference excludes all second-query locations on the wrong side, and a degree-three Bernstein coefficient one-sign-change proof establishes a unique global follow-up threshold. Evaluation at the posterior median yields a strictly negative cubic, proving the nonmedian inequality. The unrestricted nonadaptive four-outcome formula has a uniform weak-channel expansion and a unique leading optimum at two repeated midpoints, forcing the stated fourth-order gain. Finite posterior-integral and numerical checks (3,743) support but do not replace the proof. Scope explicitly fixes the first query.

value.rationale: For the natural finite-budget task of localizing a uniform continuous target using two noisy yes/no threshold measurements, the established entropy-optimal posterior median is strictly suboptimal for mean-square error. The unique squared-loss-optimal nonmedian feedback threshold and sharp e^4/32 improvement over every precommitted threshold pair are a concrete structural and quantitative result; the distinction directly guides adaptive sensor/query placement under squared-error risk.
